title: Desk screening of hydrothermal-alteration indicators around Mahd adh Dhahab from Landsat 9

headline.label: concentration of iron-oxide and clay overlap near the two Mahd adh Dhahab records

service.name: Lithological and Alteration Mapping from Satellite Imagery

data: Landsat 9 OLI-2 Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance, scene LC09_L2SP_169044_20261001_02_T1 (1 October 2026, path 169 row 44, scene cloud 0.0%, sun elevation 56.7°), bands B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7 and QA_PIXEL at 30 m.
method: Searched Landsat 8 and 9 scenes with less than 1% cloud over the window from 2024 to November 2026, and picked the clear Landsat 9 scene of 1 October 2026 (sun elevation 57°).
Read a 30 × 30 km window (EPSG:32637, x 675015 to 705015, y 2585015 to 2615015), 1,000 × 1,000 pixels, and converted it to reflectance: value × 0.0000275 − 0.2.
Masked cloud, cloud shadow and water from QA_PIXEL, vegetation (NDVI above 0.25) and dark pixels (reflectance below 0.01): 0.07% of the window.
Ratios: iron oxide B4/B2, clay, hydroxyl minerals and carbonate B6/B7, ferrous iron B6/B5.
limits: This is a desk screening that suggests where field work could start. It is not a mineral discovery, a prospect evaluation or a resource estimate, and a geologist must check it in the field. Pixels are 30 m and Landsat has only two short-wave infrared bands, so the clay ratio groups clays, micas and carbonates and cannot name a mineral.
